source.title: Emotional shaping of spatial encoding along the dorsal ventral axis of the hippocampus

confidence_rationale: Recent, well-scoped mini-review by a group whose primary work is in this exact area, synthesising the dorsoventral literature MECH-143 and MECH-144 jointly partition. Source quality 0.70 -- a review, so secondary, and Frontiers rather than a top-tier venue. Mapping fidelity 0.60: it surveys the dorsal valence literature broadly rather than isolating the value-at-fixed-location manipulation MECH-143 actually asserts. Net 0.58. NOTE: the same source is assessed separately against MECH-144, where its direction is 'mixed' -- see the paired entry in targeted_review_connectome_mech_144.
failure_signatures: The review's own summary position is that dorsal hippocampal place cells remap in response to aversive and rewarding stimuli and thereby embed valence-related information within a spatially anchored framework -- the direct contrary of a value-free dorsal map.
Aversive events such as footshock or predator odour induce dorsal remapping with NO physical change to the environment, so dorsal map stability cannot be attributed to environmental constancy.
Place fields concentrate around emotionally salient regions (both appetitive and aversive), described in the review as goal-directed remapping.

A subset of dorsal neurons is selectively activated at reward sites regardless of spatial position ('reward cells'), encoding positive valence independently of spatial context within the dorsal compartment itself.

mapping.source_claim_statement: The dorsal hippocampus maintains a high-precision spatial map that nonetheless incorporates the locations of positive and negative events; dorsal place cells remap in response to aversive and rewarding stimuli, embedding valence-related information within a spatially anchored framework, while the ventral hippocampus carries coarser spatial coding with far stronger emotional modulation.
mapping.ree_translation: The dorsal half of REE's Q-020 Path A resolution does not hold in the strong form MECH-143 states it. The review's synthesis is that the dorsal compartment embeds valence in its map rather than excluding it, which means the dorsal/ventral split cannot be drawn as value-free/value-laden. The defensible version of the split is quantitative, not categorical: dorsal carries valence at high spatial precision and low weight, ventral at low spatial precision and high weight. ARC-007's no-new-value-computation constraint has to be re-derived on that gradient rather than inherited from a clean dissociation.
mapping.mapping_caveat: A mini-review, so every finding cited here is second-hand and the primary sources have not been independently assessed in this entry -- weight it as synthesis, not as data. It also does not isolate the specific manipulation MECH-143 asserts (value varied at a constant goal location), so it does not directly refute Duvelle et al.; it refutes the broader generalisation REE drew FROM Duvelle et al. Rodent literature throughout, with the primate work MECH-144 leans on not covered.
mapping.source_context: Mini-review synthesising rodent electrophysiology, calcium imaging and optogenetics on spatial and emotional coding across the hippocampal dorsoventral axis.

confidence_components.notes: Secondary source, so source_quality is capped below the primary papers in this directory despite the review being recent and directly on-topic.
